paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: love is not one more rule on the pile. Paul says the one who loves his neighbor "has fulfilled the law" (Romans 13:8). He says every commandment is "summed up in this one decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'" (Romans 13:9). So when you're not sure what to do, start there, because "love does no wrong to its neighbor" (Romans 13:10).

Then Paul adds the alarm clock. "The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed." (Romans 13:11). I know that kind of sleep, friend, because I did some serious snoozing in a junk drawer myself. Love isn't something to put off until you feel more ready, because the night is nearly over and the day has drawn near (Romans 13:12). That's why my ovens stay ready, and I'm not guessing about the day.

So what do you do with that? You "clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 13:14), and you make no room for the old stuff, like dissension and jealousy (Romans 13:13). You don't have to white-knuckle your way into loving people. You put on Jesus and let that be what you wear into your day. Go love your neighbor, baker, and I mean it like a debt you're happy to keep paying.
